methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Mitra Chem is a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Vivas Kumar and Will Chueh that has raised $60M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparator (LNZA) operating in the same sector and stage window, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method uses the $60M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying a valuation of $114M. The peer-median method examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $700M to $3.0B (median: $1.0B), suggesting a $1.0B implied value. The median of these two methods yields $557M, with a low bound of $97M and a high bound of $1.1B.

The wide range reflects material stage and technology-maturity dispersion within the peer set. The peer-median approach is sensitive to the choice of comparables; the three selected peers (all Series C) command higher valuations than current-stage benchmarks would suggest. Key uncertainties include Mitra Chem's technical validation stage, capital efficiency relative to peers, and path to commercial deployment. A valuation in the $400M–$700M range appears most defensible absent additional operational or market data.
